description.narrative:
UN Women Mali har inkommit med en begäran till ambassaden om ett svenskt stöd uppgående till 60 miljoner kronor för att utföra den nämnda landstrategin och programmet för perioden 2016-2018. Men då genomförandet av det maliska fredsavtalet drabbat av förseningar har UN Women Mali beslutat att förlänga programmet till 2021 och det svenska stödet ska därför avse stöd till aktiviteter fram till och med den 30 juni 2021 relaterat till den aktuella förlängningen. En promemoria från UN Women Mali med denna information utgör en bilaga till det aktuella insatsavtalet. Programmet kommer att ses över och uppdateras årligen under denna period i syfte att anpassa den till de ändrade förutsättningarna för landet och i överensstämmelse med de definierade insatsområdena. Landprogrammet kommer också att uppdateras med den nya globala strategin för UN Women planerad till 2019.
Insatsavtalet med UN Women är giltigt till och med den 31 december 2021 för att UN Women ska kunna slutföra sina åtaganden avseende bl.a. rapportering efter att implementeringsperioden upphört. Avtalet baseras på en avtalsmall som är fastställd av Sida (ärendenr 15/001441).
Programmet har tre resultatområden: Resultatområde 1: Att kvinnors, särskilt de fattigaste och mest utsatta för utanförskap, ekonomiska egenmakt stärks och likaså deras motståndskraft i förhållande till miljö- och klimatpåverkan samt att de har möjlighet att dra nytta av utveckling; Resultatområde 2: Kvinnor och flickor lever ett liv fritt från våld; Resultatområde 3: Fred och säkerhet och humanitära insatser är formade av kvinnors ledarskap och delaktighet.
Insatsens totala budget är 33 miljoner US-dollar (USD), d.v.s. cirka 298 miljoner kronor, varav UN Women Mali begär extern finansiering med 23 miljoner USD (cirka 209 miljoner kronor). UN Womens huvudkontor bidrar till finansieringen med 10 miljoner USD. Sverige kommer att ge ett tematiskt stöd till programmet med ett bidrag på 60 miljoner kronor. Svenska medel kommer att blandas med bidrag från andra givare som tas emot av UN Women Mali. Givare som för närvarande deltar i finansieringen är: 1) Tyskland med 1,7 miljoner USD med ett åtagande för fyra år; Belgien med 1,7 miljoner USD för tre år; Danmark med 3,9 miljoner USD under tre år och Luxemburg med 4.4 miljoner USD för fyra år.

UN Women Mali has applied to the Embassy for funding of 60 million SEK to carry out its Country Strategy and Program initially during the period 2016-2018. However, as mentioned, as the Country Strategy and Program has a focus among other on Women’s effective participation in decision making relating to the consolidation of peace, humanitarian assistance, and given the delay of the implementation of the peace agreement, UN Women Mali has operated a shift in the initial period 2016-2018 to 2016-2021. An intra-office memorandum with this information is annexed to the current decision. The program will be reviewed and updated annually during this period in order to adapt it to the changing context of the country and in coherence with the defined areas of intervention. The country program will also be up-dated with the new global strategy of UN-Women scheduled for 2019. The activity period of the agreement is from 2016 to 30 June 2021. The agreement will be valid until 31 December 2021.
Impact areas pursued by the program are threefold: Impact Area 1: Women, especially the poorest and most excluded, are economically empowered, are resilient in a changing climate and benefit from development; Impact Area 2: Women and girls live a life free from violence; Impact Area 3: Peace and security and humanitarian action are shaped by women leadership and participation.
The intervention's total budget is USD 33 million approximately SEK 298 million of which UN Women Mali is requesting USD 23 million (approximately SEK 209 million). UN Women headquarter contributes to the funding for USD 10 million. Sweden will provide a thematic support to the program with a contribution of 60 million SEK. Swedish fund will be commingled with contributions from other donors received by UN Women Mali. The donors currently participating in the funding are: 1) Germany USD 1.7 million with a commitment for four years; Belgium USD 1.7 million for three years; Denmark USD 3.9 million for three years and Luxembourg USD 4.4 million for four years.
Women are empowered to lead, participate in, influence and contribute to national development as well as in humanitarian action and peace processes.

sector.narrative: Women’s rights organisations and movements, and government institutions

description.narrative: Between 2016 to 2021, significant results have been achieved by the program. Some results based on UN Women's areas of intervention are set out below: 1) Gender and Governance At the government level, the percentage had increased from 10 to 11.76% between 2012 and 2013. The first Government of the 2nd term of the President of the Republic, put in place in September 2018, granted 11 ministerial positions to women out of a total of 32 ministers, or 34.37%. At the level of the National Assembly, the level of representation of women in 2020 increased to 27.89%, thus approaching the minimum representation rate of 30%, set by Law No. 2015052 of December 18, 2015, instituting measures to promote gender in access to nominative and elective posts. Between 2013 and 2018 this level of representativeness was on average 9.52%. The rate of women elected to local decision-making bodies increased from 9% in 2009 to 25.56% in 2016. At the level of judicial bodies, the level of representation of women is 41.02% at the Supreme Court and 22.22% at the Constitutional Court. The Constitutional Court has been chaired by a woman (March 2015 to July 2020). Currently, women make up 26.4% of the CNT (National Transition Council). 2) Women's Economic Empowerment Through the support of UN Women, the National Bank for Agricultural Development (BNDA) has established a preferential interest rate of 8% for women. 4 centers "BuyFromWomen" (BFW) with installed computer equipment and solar energy facilitate women's access to ICTs. At least 14 communal land management charters incorporate women's land rights involving more than 289 villages in the various communes. 8,200 women are now competent in the procedures for acquiring agricultural land and are able to conduct advocacy actions to preserve their land rights. Thus, 349.822 ha have been acquired for 137 groups of 12,146 beneficiaries, of which 269.82 ha have been secured for 125 groups of 10,742 beneficiaries. 3) Gender Based-Violence (GBV) The SOPs (Standard Operation Procedures) have been updated in order to make the GBV victim management process efficient and uniform. 5 structures of the national police have received office and computer equipment in order to improve the reception and management of GBV cases as well as the collection and sharing of data on GBV survivors. 100 villages in Koulikoro and Sikasso regions have setup GBV awareness committees and have benefited from knowledge building on gender equality. 4) Women, Peace and Security (WPC) Women's political participation in peace processes is promoted: 9 women (31%) participate as members in the Follow-up Committee of the Agreement for Peace and Reconciliation in Mali following the Algiers process (CSA). As regards other peace mechanisms, in 2021, there were five female members of the Truth, Justice and Reconciliation Commission (20%) and two female members of the National Commission for Disarmament, Demobilization and Reintegration (2.6%). Women comprised 6% of the National Council for Security Sector Reform and 4% of the Monitoring Committee subcommittees. The decision of the 5th High Level Session in Kidal in February 2021 to increase the number of women on the subcommittees by 12 has not yet been implemented. Women's representation remains minimal in the decentralized government apparatus, at 1% at the regional level and 5% in the Bamako district. Women are active participants in overcoming the social and political crisis of 2020 and the political transition. Women leaders from five networks of women's civil society organizations are actively involved in Mali's political transition: the African Women Leaders Network (AWLN), the Women Leaders of Mali Platform, the ECOWAS Women's Peace and Security Network (REPSFECO), the Network of Women Former Ministers and Parliamentarians (REFAMP) and the Advocacy and Mediation Network responsible for monitoring women's participation in the peace agreement. They share an agenda and have enhanced their skills to enable them to make a substantial contribution to the reform processes, advocate gender mainstreaming in the reforms and encourage respect for Act No. 2015-052. 27 peace huts have been built, fitted out or renovated in Mopti, Douentza, Timbuktu, Goundam, Diré, Gao, Bourem and Ménaka. These are equipped and secure spaces where women can gather and talk, and access information and training opportunities. They can also be used by women as workshops to make and display handicrafts and food items. 5) Leadership, empowerment, access and protection (LEAP) in the responses to the crises The agenda and programming for humanitarian coordination has become more gender-sensitive at the national and local levels. The Gender with Age Marker (GAM) tool can now be used by 288 humanitarian actors (including 95 women) based in Segou, Mopti, Bamako, Gao, Timbuktu and Kidal, including cluster coordinators, cluster members (notably for water, sanitation and hygiene WASH), government representatives, Cluster Gender Focal Point Network and EHP member NGOs. 11,581 internally displaced persons (including 7,077 women) in the camps for internally displaced persons in Mopti and Segou, Niono, Sikasso, Gao and Bamako have received 1,158 household kits containing dignity kits for their urgent domestic needs (such as mosquito nets, soap, mats, clothes, water storage containers, cups and pots) and 1,200 kits to support income-generating activities, including equipment for market-gardening, soap-making, sewing and processing local food products.
